```{r}
### 4D. COMPREHENSIVE COMPARISON: ALL POLLUTANTS ACROSS REDLINING GRADES ###
cat("\n\n4D. COMPREHENSIVE COMPARISON: ALL POLLUTANTS VS REDLINING\n")
cat("===========================================================\n\n")

# Combine all three pollutant datasets
combined_pollutants <- bind_rows(
  pm25_redlining %>%
    dplyr::select(site, timestamp_day, housing_grade, aqi_pm25_corrected, land_use_type, population_density) %>%
    dplyr::rename(aqi_value = aqi_pm25_corrected) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pollutant = "PM2.5"),
  
  pm10_redlining %>%
    dplyr::select(site, timestamp_day, housing_grade, aqi_pm10_corrected, land_use_type, population_density) %>%
    dplyr::rename(aqi_value = aqi_pm10_corrected) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pollutant = "PM10"),
  
  ozone_redlining %>%
    dplyr::select(site, timestamp_day, housing_grade, aqi_ozone_corrected, land_use_type, population_density) %>%
    dplyr::rename(aqi_value = aqi_ozone_corrected) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pollutant = "Ozone")
)

# Clean data: Set any negative AQI values to 0 (result of corrections)
cat("Checking for negative AQI values from corrections...\n")
negative_count <- sum(combined_pollutants$aqi_value < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("  Found", negative_count, "negative AQI values\n")

if (negative_count > 0) {
  cat("  Setting negative values to 0 (standard practice)\n")
  combined_pollutants <- combined_pollutants %>%
    dplyr::mutate(aqi_value = ifelse(aqi_value < 0, 0, aqi_value))
}

# Summary statistics by pollutant and redlining grade
cat("\nSummary statistics by pollutant and redlining grade:\n")
summary_stats <- combined_pollutants %>%
  group_by(pollutant, housing_grade) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_aqi = round(mean(aqi_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    median_aqi = round(median(aqi_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    sd_aqi = round(sd(aqi_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    min_aqi = round(min(aqi_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_aqi = round(max(aqi_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )
print(summary_stats)

# 4D.1. Generate significance letters for each pollutant
cat("\n4D.1. Generating significance letters for each pollutant...\n")

# Run ANOVA and Tukey HSD for each pollutant
all_letters <- list()

for (poll in c("PM2.5", "PM10", "Ozone")) {
  cat("  Processing", poll, "...\n")
  
  # Filter data for this pollutant and remove NAs in model variables
  pollutant_data <- combined_pollutants %>% 
    filter(pollutant == poll) %>%
    filter(!is.na(aqi_value), !is.na(housing_grade), !is.na(population_density))
  
  if (nrow(pollutant_data) < 5) {
    cat("    Insufficient data for", poll, " (n < 5). Skipping analysis.\n")
    next
  }

  # Ensure factors have proper levels
  pollutant_data$housing_grade <- factor(pollutant_data$housing_grade, 
                                         levels = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "IC", "Not Graded"))
  
  # Count distinct levels to avoid the "contrasts" error
  h_levels <- n_distinct(pollutant_data$housing_grade)
  
  if (h_levels >= 2) {
    # Run ANOVA
    poll_anova <- aov(aqi_value ~ housing_grade + population_density, 
                      data = pollutant_data)
    poll_anova_summary <- summary(poll_anova)
    
    # Check if significant
    p_val <- poll_anova_summary[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
    if (!is.null(p_val) && !is.na(p_val) && p_val < 0.05) {
      # Run Tukey HSD
      tukey_result <- TukeyHSD(poll_anova, "housing_grade")
      
      cat("    Tukey HSD p-values for", poll, ":\n")
      print(tukey_result$housing_grade[, "p adj"])
      
      # Generate letters using multcompView
      tukey_p_values <- tukey_result$housing_grade[, "p adj"]
      
      # Extract group names from row names of Tukey results
      comparison_names <- rownames(tukey_result$housing_grade)
      names(tukey_p_values) <- comparison_names
      
      letters_result <- multcompLetters(tukey_p_values)
      
      # Create dataframe with letters
      letters_df <- data.frame(
        housing_grade = names(letters_result$Letters),
        letters = as.character(letters_result$Letters),
        pollutant = poll,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      
      cat("    Significance letters for", poll, ":\n")
      print(letters_df)
      
      all_letters[[poll]] <- letters_df
    } else {
      # No significant differences
      cat("    No significant differences for", poll, "\n")
      unique_grades <- levels(pollutant_data$housing_grade)
      unique_grades <- unique_grades[unique_grades %in% unique(pollutant_data$housing_grade)]
      
      letters_df <- data.frame(
        housing_grade = unique_grades,
        letters = "a",
        pollutant = poll,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      all_letters[[poll]] <- letters_df
    }
  } else {
    cat("    Insufficient distinct levels for ANOVA for", poll, ".\n")
    unique_grades <- levels(pollutant_data$housing_grade)
    unique_grades <- unique_grades[unique_grades %in% unique(pollutant_data$housing_grade)]
    
    letters_df <- data.frame(
      housing_grade = unique_grades,
      letters = "a",
      pollutant = poll,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    all_letters[[poll]] <- letters_df
  }
}

# Combine all letters
combined_letters <- bind_rows(all_letters)

# Ensure columns exist if empty
if (nrow(combined_letters) == 0) {
  combined_letters <- data.frame(housing_grade = factor(), letters = character(), pollutant = character(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

if (nrow(combined_letters) > 0) {
  # Calculate y-positions for letters (dynamically above the data)
  y_positions <- combined_pollutants %>%
    group_by(pollutant, housing_grade) %>%
    summarise(
      max_aqi = max(aqi_value, na.rm = TRUE),
      q75 = quantile(aqi_value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      iqr = IQR(aqi_value, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop'
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Position above upper whisker or max value
      whisker_top = q75 + 1.8 * iqr,
      y_pos = pmax(whisker_top, max_aqi) * 1.05 + 2
    )

  # Merge letters with y-positions
  combined_letters <- combined_letters %>%
    left_join(y_positions, by = c("pollutant", "housing_grade"))
} else {
  combined_letters$y_pos <- numeric()
}

cat("Significance letters generated.\n")
print(combined_letters)

# 4D.2. Faceted violin plot comparison with significance letters
cat("\n4D.2. Creating faceted violin plot comparison with significance letters...\n")

# Define HOLC redlining map colors
holc_colors <- c(
  "A" = "#4CAF50",           # Green (Best)
  "B" = "#2196F3",           # Blue (Still Desirable)
  "C" = "#FFC107",           # Yellow/Amber (Declining)
  "D" = "#F44336",           # Red (Hazardous)
  "IC" = "#89C4E1",          # Light Blue (Industrial/Commercial)
  "Not Graded" = "#757575",  # Dark Gray (Not Graded)
  "C: Declining" = "#FFC107",
  "D: Hazardous" = "#F44336",
  "IC: Industrial" = "#89C4E1",
  "Not Graded" = "#757575"
)

# Add descriptive labels to combined data
combined_pollutants_labeled <- combined_pollutants %>%
  mutate(housing_grade_label = case_when(
    housing_grade == "C" ~ "C: Declining",
    housing_grade == "D" ~ "D: Hazardous",
    housing_grade == "IC" ~ "IC: Industrial",
    housing_grade == "Not Graded" ~ "Not Graded",
    TRUE ~ as.character(housing_grade)
  )) %>%
  mutate(housing_grade_label = factor(housing_grade_label, 
                                      levels = c("C: Declining", "D: Hazardous", "IC: Industrial", "Not Graded")))

# Update combined letters to use labeled grades
combined_letters_labeled <- combined_letters %>%
  mutate(housing_grade_label = case_when(
    housing_grade == "C" ~ "C: Declining",
    housing_grade == "D" ~ "D: Hazardous",
    housing_grade == "IC" ~ "IC: Industrial",
    housing_grade == "Not Graded" ~ "Not Graded",
    TRUE ~ as.character(housing_grade)
  ))

pollutant_comparison_violin <- ggplot(combined_pollutants_labeled, 
                                       aes(x = housing_grade_label, y = aqi_value, fill = housing_grade_label)) +
  geom_violin(color = "white", lwd = 0.8, alpha = 0.8, trim = FALSE) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", shape = 21, size = 2.5, 
               fill = "white", color = "black", stroke = 1) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.05, size = 0.3, color = "black") +
  
  # Add significance letters - larger and more prominent
  geom_text(data = combined_letters_labeled, 
            aes(x = housing_grade_label, y = y_pos, label = letters),
            size = 7, fontface = "bold", color = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  
  facet_wrap(~pollutant, ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Historic housing grade",
    y = "Air Quality Index (AQI)",
    fill = "Redlining Grade"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = holc_colors) 

print(pollutant_comparison_violin)

cat("\n=============================================================================\n")
cat("COMPREHENSIVE COMPARISON COMPLETE\n")
cat("=============================================================================\n\n")

```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PM10 ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================
cat("\n--- PM10 AQI Analysis ---\n\n")

# For each day, fit a spatial lag model to understand social vulnerability effects on PM10
# OPTIMIZED: Use parallel processing for day-by-day models (biggest performance gain)
cat("Fitting spatial lag models for PM10 (parallel processing enabled)...\n")
# For each day, fit a spatial lag model to understand social vulnerability effects on PM10
cat("Fitting spatial lag models for PM10 (parallel processing enabled)...\n")
results_by_day_pm10 <- run_daily_spatial_regression(daily_avg, "aqi_pm10_corrected")

# Effect of social vulnerability on PM10 AQI over time (controlling for population density and land use)
results_by_day_pm10 %>% 
  filter(model_fit == "Success") %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = coef_social_vuln)) +
  geom_line(color = "gray50", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(color = coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05, size = coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "gray", "TRUE" = "red"), 
                     labels = c("Not significant", "Significant")) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 1, "TRUE" = 2)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(
    x = "Date",
    y = "Social Vulnerability Coefficient",
    color = "Significance (p < 0.05)",
    size = "Significance (p < 0.05)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "2 months",
              limits = c(as.Date("2024-12-01"), as.Date("2026-12-31"))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1, 1))  # Adjust limits as needed

# 2. Plot spatial autocorrelation (rho) over time for PM10
results_by_day_pm10 %>% 
  filter(model_fit == "Success") %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = rho)) +
  geom_line(color = "gray50", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(color = rho_p < 0.05, size = rho_p < 0.05)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "gray", "TRUE" = "blue"), 
                     labels = c("Not significant", "Significant")) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 1, "TRUE" = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Date",
    y = "Spatial Lag Parameter (rho)",
    color = "Significance (p < 0.05)",
    size = "Significance (p < 0.05)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "2 months",
              limits = c(as.Date("2024-12-01"), as.Date("2026-12-31")))

# 3. Summary of significant social vulnerability effects for PM10
cat("Summary of Social Vulnerability Effects on PM10 AQI:\n")
cat("=====================================================\n")

significant_days_pm10 <- results_by_day_pm10 %>% 
  filter(model_fit == "Success", coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05)

  cat("Days with significant social vulnerability effect:", nrow(significant_days_pm10), "out of", 
      nrow(results_by_day_pm10 %>% filter(model_fit == "Success")), "\n")
  
  success_count_pm10 <- nrow(results_by_day_pm10 %>% filter(model_fit == "Success"))
  cat("Percentage of days with significant effect:", 
      ifelse(success_count_pm10 > 0, round(nrow(significant_days_pm10) / success_count_pm10 * 100, 1), 0), "%\n\n")

if (nrow(significant_days_pm10) > 0) {
  cat("Summary of significant effects:\n")
  print(summary(significant_days_pm10$coef_social_vuln))
  
  cat("\nDirection of effects:\n")
  cat("Positive effects (worse air quality in vulnerable areas):", 
      sum(significant_days_pm10$coef_social_vuln > 0), "days\n")
  cat("Negative effects (better air quality in vulnerable areas):", 
      sum(significant_days_pm10$coef_social_vuln < 0), "days\n")
}

# 4. Monthly averages to identify seasonal patterns for PM10
monthly_effects_pm10 <- results_by_day_pm10 %>%
  filter(model_fit == "Success") %>%
  mutate(month = month(date), year = year(date)) %>%
  group_by(year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_coef = mean(coef_social_vuln, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_coef_sig = mean(coef_social_vuln[coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05], na.rm = TRUE),
    n_days = n(),
    n_sig_days = sum(coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(month_year = paste(year, month, sep = "-"))

ggplot(monthly_effects_pm10, aes(x = month_year, y = mean_coef)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = n_sig_days > 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "gray", "TRUE" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average Social Vulnerability Effect on PM10 AQI",
    subtitle = "Red bars = months with at least one significant day",
    x = "Month-Year",
    y = "Average Social Vulnerability Coefficient",
    fill = "Has Significant Days"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12))

# 5. Model diagnostics for PM10
cat("\nPM10 Model Diagnostics:\n")
cat("==================\n")
model_summary_pm10 <- results_by_day_pm10 %>%
  filter(model_fit == "Success") %>%
  summarise(
    total_days = n(),
    successful_models = sum(model_fit == "Success"),
    avg_sites_per_model = mean(n_sites, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_sites = min(n_sites, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_sites = max(n_sites, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(model_summary_pm10)

# 6. Identify specific time periods with strongest social vulnerability effects for PM10
cat("\nTime Periods with Strongest Social Vulnerability Effects (PM10):\n")
cat("========================================================\n")

# Top 10 days with strongest positive effects (worse air quality in vulnerable areas)
top_positive_effects_pm10 <- results_by_day_pm10 %>%
  filter(model_fit == "Success", coef_social_vuln > 0, coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(desc(coef_social_vuln)) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, coef_social_vuln, coef_social_vuln_p, rho, rho_p, n_sites)

cat("Top 10 days with strongest positive effects (worse air quality in vulnerable areas):\n")
print(top_positive_effects_pm10)

# Top 10 days with strongest negative effects (better air quality in vulnerable areas)
top_negative_effects_pm10 <- results_by_day_pm10 %>%
  filter(model_fit == "Success", coef_social_vuln < 0, coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(coef_social_vuln) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, coef_social_vuln, coef_social_vuln_p, rho, rho_p, n_sites)

cat("\nTop 10 days with strongest negative effects (better air quality in vulnerable areas):\n")
print(top_negative_effects_pm10)

# 7. Seasonal analysis for PM10
seasonal_effects_pm10 <- results_by_day_pm10 %>%
  filter(model_fit == "Success") %>%
  mutate(
    season = get_season_year(date)
  ) %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(
    n_days = n(),
    n_sig_days = sum(coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_coef = mean(coef_social_vuln, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_coef_sig = mean(coef_social_vuln[coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_rho = mean(rho, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\nSeasonal Analysis of Social Vulnerability Effects (PM10):\n")
print(seasonal_effects_pm10)

    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("Population Density Effects:\n")
cat("Days with significant population density effect:", pop_density_summary_pm10$n_sig_pop_density, 
    "out of", pop_density_summary_pm10$n_days, "\n")
cat("Average population density coefficient:", round(pop_density_summary_pm10$mean_pop_density_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("Average significant population density coefficient:", round(pop_density_summary_pm10$mean_pop_density_coef_sig, 4), "\n\n")

# Land use effects summary
land_use_summary_pm10 <- results_by_day_pm10 %>%
  filter(model_fit == "Success") %>%
  summarise(
    n_days = n(),

cat("Industrial areas - significant days:", land_use_summary_pm10$n_sig_industrial, 
    "out of", land_use_summary_pm10$n_days, "\n")

cat("Mixed use areas - significant days:", land_use_summary_pm10$n_sig_mixed, 
    "out of", land_use_summary_pm10$n_days, "\n")
cat("Mixed use areas - average coefficient:", round(land_use_summary_pm10$mean_mixed_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("Open space areas - significant days:", land_use_summary_pm10$n_sig_open, 
    "out of", land_use_summary_pm10$n_days, "\n")
cat("Open space areas - average coefficient:", round(land_use_summary_pm10$mean_open_coef, 4), "\n")

  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "2 months",
              limits = c(as.Date("2024-12-01"), as.Date("2026-12-31")))
```

#####4f. When do different vulnerability areas have worse AQI? (High, Moderate, Low - After all controls)

```{r}
cat("=============================================================================\n")
cat("4F. WHEN DO DIFFERENT VULNERABILITY AREAS EXPERIENCE POOR AIR QUALITY?\n")
cat("(High, Moderate, and Low Vulnerability - After all controls)\n")
cat("(After controlling for population density and land use)\n")
cat("=============================================================================\n\n")

# Function to analyze vulnerability effects for a given pollutant
# Now includes High, Moderate, and Low vulnerability categories
# Updated to handle multiple years (Winter 2024-25 vs Winter 2025-26, etc.)
analyze_vulnerability_effects <- function(results_data, pollutant_name) {
  vulnerability_effects <- results_data %>%
    filter(model_fit == "Success") %>%
    mutate(
      month_name = month.name[month(date)],
      year = year(date),
      # Use the standardized helper for consistency
      season = get_season_year(date)
    )
  
  # Categorize vulnerability effects based on coefficient direction and significance
  # The coefficient coef_social_vuln represents: higher social vulnerability → effect on AQI
  # Positive coefficient = higher vulnerability associated with worse AQI
  # Negative coefficient = higher vulnerability associated with better AQI (or low vulnerability areas have worse AQI)
  
  # Categorize vulnerability effects into High, Moderate, and Low vulnerability categories
  # Calculate thresholds based on coefficient magnitude (for significant positive coefficients)
  sig_positive_coefs <- vulnerability_effects$coef_social_vuln[vulnerability_effects$coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05 & vulnerability_effects$coef_social_vuln > 0]
  if (length(sig_positive_coefs) > 0) {
    # Use tertiles to split positive significant coefficients into High and Moderate
    high_threshold <- quantile(sig_positive_coefs, 0.67, na.rm = TRUE)  # Top third
    moderate_threshold <- quantile(sig_positive_coefs, 0.33, na.rm = TRUE)  # Bottom third
  } else {
    # Default thresholds if no positive significant coefficients
    high_threshold <- 0.1
    moderate_threshold <- 0.05
  }
  
  vulnerability_effects <- vulnerability_effects %>%
    mutate(
      # HIGH VULNERABILITY WORSE: Large positive significant coefficient (top third)
      high_vuln_sig = coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05 & coef_social_vuln > high_threshold,
      
      # MODERATE VULNERABILITY WORSE: Small positive significant coefficient (bottom two-thirds)
      moderate_vuln_sig = coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05 & coef_social_vuln > 0 & coef_social_vuln <= high_threshold,
      
      # LOW VULNERABILITY WORSE: Negative significant coefficient
      low_vuln_sig = coef_social_vuln_p < 0.05 & coef_social_vuln < 0
    )
  
  # Overall summary
  overall_summary <- vulnerability_effects %>%
    summarise(
      total_days = n(),
      # High vulnerability category (large positive significant coefficient)
      days_high_vuln_sig = sum(high_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_high_vuln_sig = round(days_high_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1),
      # Moderate vulnerability category (small positive significant coefficient)
      days_moderate_vuln_sig = sum(moderate_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_moderate_vuln_sig = round(days_moderate_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1),
      # Low vulnerability category (negative significant coefficient)
      days_low_vuln_sig = sum(low_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_low_vuln_sig = round(days_low_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1)
    )
  
  # Seasonal analysis
  seasonal_summary <- vulnerability_effects %>%
    group_by(season) %>%
    summarise(
      total_days = n(),
      # High vulnerability category (large positive significant coefficient)
      days_high_vuln_sig = sum(high_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_high_vuln_sig = round(days_high_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1),
      # Moderate vulnerability category (small positive significant coefficient)
      days_moderate_vuln_sig = sum(moderate_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_moderate_vuln_sig = round(days_moderate_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1),
      # Low vulnerability category (negative significant coefficient)
      days_low_vuln_sig = sum(low_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_low_vuln_sig = round(days_low_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(pct_high_vuln_sig))
  
  # Monthly analysis
  monthly_summary <- vulnerability_effects %>%
    group_by(month_name) %>%
    summarise(
      total_days = n(),
      # High vulnerability category (large positive significant coefficient)
      days_high_vuln_sig = sum(high_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_high_vuln_sig = round(days_high_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1),
      # Moderate vulnerability category (small positive significant coefficient)
      days_moderate_vuln_sig = sum(moderate_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_moderate_vuln_sig = round(days_moderate_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1),
      # Low vulnerability category (negative significant coefficient)
      days_low_vuln_sig = sum(low_vuln_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_low_vuln_sig = round(days_low_vuln_sig / total_days * 100, 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(pct_high_vuln_sig))
  
  return(list(
    overall = overall_summary,
    seasonal = seasonal_summary,
    monthly = monthly_summary,
    daily_data = vulnerability_effects
  ))
}

                        pm10_results$overall$pct_low_vuln_sig,
                        ozone_results$overall$pct_low_vuln_sig)
)

# Extract date ranges for each season from daily data

season_date_ranges <- pm25_results$daily_data %>%

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

    # Format dates: use abbreviated month names

    end_month = format(max_date, "%b"),

    end_date_str = paste0(end_month, ". ", end_year),
    # Create season label with date range

  ) %>%

cat("\nSeason date ranges:\n")

# Parse season names to get year and season type for sorting
season_order <- tibble(season = all_seasons) %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract season type (Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall)
    season_type = str_extract(season, "^(Winter|Spring|Summer|Fall)"),
    # Extract year(s)
    year_part = str_extract(season, "\\d{4}"),
    # For Winter with format "Winter YYYY-YYYY", extract first year
    year_num = as.numeric(ifelse(str_detect(season, "\\d{4}-\\d{4}"),
                                  str_extract(season, "\\d{4}(?=-)"),
                                  year_part)),
    # Season type order within year
    season_type_order = case_when(
      season_type == "Winter" ~ 1,
      season_type == "Spring" ~ 2,
      season_type == "Summer" ~ 3,
      season_type == "Fall" ~ 4
    ),
    # Combined sort key
    sort_key = year_num * 10 + season_type_order
  ) %>%
  arrange(sort_key) %>%
  pull(season)

vulnerability_comparison <- combined_seasonal %>%
  dplyr::select(Pollutant, season, pct_high_vuln_sig, pct_moderate_vuln_sig, pct_low_vuln_sig,
                days_high_vuln_sig, days_moderate_vuln_sig, days_low_vuln_sig, total_days) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pct_high_vuln_sig, pct_moderate_vuln_sig, pct_low_vuln_sig),
    names_to = "vulnerability_category",
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    vulnerability_category = case_when(
      vulnerability_category == "pct_high_vuln_sig" ~ "High",
      vulnerability_category == "pct_moderate_vuln_sig" ~ "Moderate",
      vulnerability_category == "pct_low_vuln_sig" ~ "Low"
    ),
    vulnerability_category = factor(vulnerability_category, levels = c("High", "Moderate", "Low")),
    Pollutant = factor(Pollutant, levels = c("PM2.5", "PM10", "Ozone")),
    season = factor(season, levels = season_order)
  )

# Calculate significance tests for differences between vulnerability categories within each season-pollutant combination
# Use chi-square test of proportions
cat("\n=== SIGNIFICANCE TESTS: Differences Between Vulnerability Categories Within Each Season ===\n")
significance_results <- vulnerability_comparison %>%
  group_by(Pollutant, season) %>%
  summarise(
    high_days = first(days_high_vuln_sig),
    moderate_days = first(days_moderate_vuln_sig),
    low_days = first(days_low_vuln_sig),
    total = first(total_days),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    # Create contingency table for chi-square test
    # Test if proportions differ significantly
    chi_sq_p = {
      # Create a matrix: success (significant days) vs failure (non-significant days) for each category
      # Note: Each category can have significant days, but they're mutually exclusive categories
      # So we test if the distribution of significant days across categories differs from expected
      observed <- c(high_days, moderate_days, low_days)
      # Expected: if all categories were equal, each would have (total/3) significant days
      # But actually, we want to test if the proportions differ
      # Use chi-square test for proportions
      if(sum(observed) > 0 && total > 0) {
        # Test if proportions are different
        # Create a 2x3 table: significant vs non-significant for each category
        sig_matrix <- matrix(c(
          high_days, total - high_days,
          moderate_days, total - moderate_days,
          low_days, total - low_days
        ), nrow = 3, ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
        
        # Chi-square test
        test_result <- tryCatch({
          chisq.test(sig_matrix)
        }, error = function(e) NULL)
        
        if(!is.null(test_result)) {
          test_result$p.value
        } else {
          NA_real_
        }
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    },
    is_significant = !is.na(chi_sq_p) && chi_sq_p < 0.05
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Print significance test results
for(i in 1:nrow(significance_results)) {
  poll <- significance_results$Pollutant[i]
  seas <- significance_results$season[i]
  p_val <- significance_results$chi_sq_p[i]
  sig <- significance_results$is_significant[i]
  
  cat("\n", poll, "-", seas, ":\n")
  if(!is.na(p_val)) {
    cat("  Chi-square test p-value:", format(p_val, digits = 4))
    if(sig) {
      cat(" * (significant differences between categories)\n")
    } else {
      cat(" (no significant differences)\n")
    }
  } else {
    cat("  Insufficient data for test\n")
  }
}

# Generate significance letters for each season-pollutant combination
# Use pairwise proportion tests when overall test is significant
significance_letters_list <- list()

for(i in 1:nrow(significance_results)) {
  poll <- as.character(significance_results$Pollutant[i])
  seas <- as.character(significance_results$season[i])
  
  if(significance_results$is_significant[i] && !is.na(significance_results$chi_sq_p[i])) {
    # Get the data for this combination
    high_days <- significance_results$high_days[i]
    moderate_days <- significance_results$moderate_days[i]
    low_days <- significance_results$low_days[i]
    total <- significance_results$total[i]
    
    # Perform pairwise proportion tests
    # High vs Moderate
    p_high_mod <- tryCatch({
      prop.test(c(high_days, moderate_days), c(total, total))$p.value
    }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
    
    # High vs Low
    p_high_low <- tryCatch({
      prop.test(c(high_days, low_days), c(total, total))$p.value
    }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
    
    # Moderate vs Low
    p_mod_low <- tryCatch({
      prop.test(c(moderate_days, low_days), c(total, total))$p.value
    }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
    
    # Assign letters based on pairwise comparisons
    # Groups that are NOT significantly different share the same letter
    letters <- c("a", "a", "a")  # Start with all same
    names(letters) <- c("High", "Moderate", "Low")
    
    # Adjust based on pairwise tests (using Bonferroni correction: p < 0.05/3 = 0.0167)
    if(!is.na(p_high_mod) && p_high_mod >= 0.0167) {
      # High and Moderate not different - keep same letter
    } else {
      # High and Moderate different - change Moderate
      letters["Moderate"] <- "b"
    }
    
    if(!is.na(p_high_low) && p_high_low >= 0.0167) {
      # High and Low not different
      if(letters["High"] == "a") {
        letters["Low"] <- "a"
      }
    } else {
      # High and Low different
      if(letters["Low"] == "a" && letters["Moderate"] == "b") {
        letters["Low"] <- "c"
      } else if(letters["Low"] == "a") {
        letters["Low"] <- "b"
      }
    }
    
    if(!is.na(p_mod_low) && p_mod_low >= 0.0167) {
      # Moderate and Low not different - make them same
      if(letters["Moderate"] == "b" && letters["Low"] == "c") {
        letters["Low"] <- "b"
      } else if(letters["Moderate"] == "a" && letters["Low"] == "b") {
        letters["Low"] <- "a"
      }
    }
    
    # Store letters
    key <- paste(poll, seas, sep = "_")
    significance_letters_list[[key]] <- letters
  } else {
    # No significant differences - all get same letter
    key <- paste(poll, seas, sep = "_")
    significance_letters_list[[key]] <- c("High" = "a", "Moderate" = "a", "Low" = "a")
  }
}

# Add significance letters to vulnerability_comparison
vulnerability_comparison <- vulnerability_comparison %>%
  mutate(
    key = paste(Pollutant, season, sep = "_"),
    sig_letter = map2_chr(key, vulnerability_category, function(k, cat) {
      if(k %in% names(significance_letters_list)) {
        significance_letters_list[[k]][as.character(cat)]
      } else {
        ""
      }
    })
  )

season_is_zero <- vuln_long %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(all_zero = all(percentage == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# ── Utility: get subtitle date range for a season ──────────────────────────
get_season_subtitle <- function(seas) {
  row <- season_date_ranges %>% filter(as.character(season) == as.character(seas))
  if (nrow(row) == 0) return("")
  # Extract from season_label which already has the "(Mon. YYYY - Mon. YYYY)" part
  lbl <- row$season_label[1]
  # Season label format: "Season YYYY\n(Mon. YYYY - Mon. YYYY)"
  date_part <- str_extract(lbl, "\\(.*\\)")
  if (is.na(date_part)) return("")
  # Strip outer parentheses
  gsub("[()]", "", date_part)
}

# ── Compute top-2 outlier values (dynamically) for annotation ───────────────
# Only annotate if value is in the top 2 overall AND ≥ 15%
top_outliers <- vuln_long %>%
  arrange(desc(percentage)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 2) %>%
  filter(percentage >= 15)

# ── Panel builder function ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
make_season_panel <- function(seas, is_bottom_row, is_left_col) {
  d <- vuln_long %>% filter(as.character(season) == as.character(seas))
  zero_panel <- season_is_zero %>% 
    filter(as.character(season) == as.character(seas)) %>% 
    pull(all_zero)

  season_title    <- as.character(seas)
  season_subtitle <- get_season_subtitle(seas)

  # Base empty panel (keeps x-axis labels consistent even for zero panels)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = Pollutant,
                     y = percentage,
                     color = vuln_label,
                     group = vuln_label)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
      "PM2.5" = "PM<sub>2.5</sub>",
      "PM10"  = "PM<sub>10</sub>",
      "Ozone" = "Ozone"
    )) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = vuln_colors,
      name   = "Vulnerability Category (Worse Air Quality)"
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 35)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 10, 20, 30)) +
    labs(
      title    = season_title,
      subtitle = season_subtitle,
      x        = if (is_bottom_row) "Pollutant" else NULL,
      y        = NULL       # shared y-label applied via patchwork
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold",   margin = margin(b = 1)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, face = "plain", margin = margin(b = 4)),
      axis.title.x  = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none"   # collected by patchwork
    )

  if (zero_panel) {
    # No lollipops — just a text annotation
    p <- p +
      annotate("text",
               x = 2, y = 17.5,
               label    = "No significant disparities detected",
               fontface = "italic",
               color    = "#888888",
               size     = 3.5)
  } else {
    p <- p +
      geom_segment(
        aes(xend = Pollutant, yend = 0),
        linewidth = 0.8,
        position  = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
      ) +
      geom_point(
        size     = 2.2,
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
      )

    # Annotate top outliers that fall in this season
    outliers_here <- top_outliers %>%
      filter(as.character(season) == seas)
    if (nrow(outliers_here) > 0) {
      p <- p +
        geom_text(
          data = outliers_here,
          aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%"), y = percentage + 1.2),
          size    = 3.2,
          position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
          show.legend = FALSE
        )
    }
  }

  p
}

# ── Build one panel per season in chronological order ──────────────────────
n_seasons <- length(all_season_order)

  seas       <- all_season_order[i]
  row_num    <- ceiling(i / n_cols)
  is_bottom  <- row_num == n_rows
  is_left    <- (i %% n_cols) == 1
  make_season_panel(seas, is_bottom, is_left)
})

# ── Combine with patchwork ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Key findings
# ============================================================================
# STATISTICAL SIGNIFICANCE TESTS FOR KEY FINDINGS
# ============================================================================
cat("\n\nSTATISTICAL TESTS FOR OVERALL PATTERNS:\n")
cat("========================================\n\n")

# Test 1: Is the proportion of significant days greater than chance (5%)?
cat("1. Binomial Tests: Are significant days more frequent than random chance (5%)?\n")
cat("   (Testing if % sig days > 5% expected from Type I error)\n\n")

# PM2.5 binomial test (using High vulnerability category)
pm25_binom <- binom.test(
  pm25_results$overall$days_high_vuln_sig, 
  pm25_results$overall$total_days, 
  p = 0.05, 
  alternative = "greater"
)
cat("   PM2.5: p =", format.pval(pm25_binom$p.value, digits = 3), 
    ifelse(pm25_binom$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n")

# PM10 binomial test (using High vulnerability category)
pm10_binom <- binom.test(
  pm10_results$overall$days_high_vuln_sig, 
  pm10_results$overall$total_days, 
  p = 0.05, 
  alternative = "greater"
)
cat("   PM10:  p =", format.pval(pm10_binom$p.value, digits = 3), 
    ifelse(pm10_binom$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n")

# Ozone binomial test (using High vulnerability category)
ozone_binom <- binom.test(
  ozone_results$overall$days_high_vuln_sig, 
  ozone_results$overall$total_days, 
  p = 0.05, 
  alternative = "greater"
)
cat("   Ozone: p =", format.pval(ozone_binom$p.value, digits = 3), 
    ifelse(ozone_binom$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n\n")

# Test 2: Are the daily coefficients significantly positive overall?
cat("2. One-Sample t-tests: Are social vulnerability coefficients significantly > 0?\n")
cat("   (Testing if average daily coefficient differs from zero)\n\n")

# PM2.5 t-test
pm25_ttest <- t.test(pm25_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, mu = 0, alternative = "greater")
cat("   PM2.5: Mean coef =", round(mean(pm25_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    ", p =", format.pval(pm25_ttest$p.value, digits = 3),
    ifelse(pm25_ttest$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n")

# PM10 t-test
pm10_ttest <- t.test(pm10_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, mu = 0, alternative = "greater")
cat("   PM10:  Mean coef =", round(mean(pm10_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    ", p =", format.pval(pm10_ttest$p.value, digits = 3),
    ifelse(pm10_ttest$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n")

# Ozone t-test
ozone_ttest <- t.test(ozone_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, mu = 0, alternative = "greater")
cat("   Ozone: Mean coef =", round(mean(ozone_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    ", p =", format.pval(ozone_ttest$p.value, digits = 3),
    ifelse(ozone_ttest$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n\n")

# Test 3: Chi-square test for seasonal differences
cat("3. Chi-Square Tests: Do significant days vary by season?\n\n")

# PM2.5 seasonal chi-square (using High vulnerability category)
pm25_seasonal_table <- table(
  Season = pm25_results$daily_data$season,
  Significant = pm25_results$daily_data$high_vuln_sig
)
pm25_chisq <- chisq.test(pm25_seasonal_table)
cat("   PM2.5: χ² =", round(pm25_chisq$statistic, 2), 
    ", p =", format.pval(pm25_chisq$p.value, digits = 3),
    ifelse(pm25_chisq$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n")

# PM10 seasonal chi-square (using High vulnerability category)
pm10_seasonal_table <- table(
  Season = pm10_results$daily_data$season,
  Significant = pm10_results$daily_data$high_vuln_sig
)
pm10_chisq <- chisq.test(pm10_seasonal_table)
cat("   PM10:  χ² =", round(pm10_chisq$statistic, 2), 
    ", p =", format.pval(pm10_chisq$p.value, digits = 3),
    ifelse(pm10_chisq$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n")

# Ozone seasonal chi-square (using High vulnerability category)
ozone_seasonal_table <- table(
  Season = ozone_results$daily_data$season,
  Significant = ozone_results$daily_data$high_vuln_sig
)
ozone_chisq <- chisq.test(ozone_seasonal_table)
cat("   Ozone: χ² =", round(ozone_chisq$statistic, 2), 
    ", p =", format.pval(ozone_chisq$p.value, digits = 3),
    ifelse(ozone_chisq$p.value < 0.05, "***SIGNIFICANT***", "(not significant)"), "\n\n")

cat("=============================================================================\n\n")

cat("KEY FINDINGS:\n")
cat("=============\n")
cat("1. PM2.5: High vulnerability category (large positive coefficient) is significant on", 
    pm25_results$overall$pct_high_vuln_sig, "% of analysis days\n")
cat("   (Binomial test: p =", format.pval(pm25_binom$p.value, digits = 3), ")\n")
cat("   - Worst season:", pm25_results$seasonal$season[1], "(", pm25_results$seasonal$pct_high_vuln_sig[1], "% of days)\n")
cat("   - Worst month:", pm25_results$monthly$month_name[1], "(", pm25_results$monthly$pct_high_vuln_sig[1], "% of days)\n")
cat("   - Overall mean coefficient:", round(mean(pm25_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, na.rm = TRUE), 4), 
    "(t-test: p =", format.pval(pm25_ttest$p.value, digits = 3), ")\n\n")

cat("2. PM10: High vulnerability category (large positive coefficient) is significant on", 
    pm10_results$overall$pct_high_vuln_sig, "% of analysis days\n")
cat("   (Binomial test: p =", format.pval(pm10_binom$p.value, digits = 3), ")\n")
cat("   - Worst season:", pm10_results$seasonal$season[1], "(", pm10_results$seasonal$pct_high_vuln_sig[1], "% of days)\n")
cat("   - Worst month:", pm10_results$monthly$month_name[1], "(", pm10_results$monthly$pct_high_vuln_sig[1], "% of days)\n")
cat("   - Overall mean coefficient:", round(mean(pm10_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, na.rm = TRUE), 4), 
    "(t-test: p =", format.pval(pm10_ttest$p.value, digits = 3), ")\n\n")

cat("3. Ozone: High vulnerability category (large positive coefficient) is significant on", 
    ozone_results$overall$pct_high_vuln_sig, "% of analysis days\n")
cat("   (Binomial test: p =", format.pval(ozone_binom$p.value, digits = 3), ")\n")
cat("   - Worst season:", ozone_results$seasonal$season[1], "(", ozone_results$seasonal$pct_high_vuln_sig[1], "% of days)\n")
cat("   - Worst month:", ozone_results$monthly$month_name[1], "(", ozone_results$monthly$pct_high_vuln_sig[1], "% of days)\n")
cat("   - Overall mean coefficient:", round(mean(ozone_results$daily_data$coef_social_vuln, na.rm = TRUE), 4), 
    "(t-test: p =", format.pval(ozone_ttest$p.value, digits = 3), ")\n\n")

cat("4. Overall Pattern: High vulnerability areas are disproportionately affected by poor air quality,\n")
cat("   with effects varying by pollutant type and season even after controlling for all spatial factors.\n")
```

```{r}
# 3. Statistical tests for disparities
cat("=== STATISTICAL TESTS FOR DISPARITIES ===\n")

# Function to extract significance letters from Tukey HSD results
get_significance_letters <- function(tukey_result, categories) {
  # Try to use multcompView package if available, otherwise use manual method
  if(requireNamespace("multcompView", quietly = TRUE)) {
    tukey_df <- as.data.frame(tukey_result$social_vuln_category)
    p_vals <- tukey_df$`p adj`
    names(p_vals) <- rownames(tukey_df)
    
    # Convert to compact letter display
    tryCatch({
      letters_result <- multcompView::multcompLetters(p_vals)
      # Convert to named vector matching categories
      result <- rep("", length(categories))
      names(result) <- categories
      for(cat in categories) {
        result[cat] <- letters_result$Letters[cat]
      }
      return(result)
    }, error = function(e) {
      # Fall back to manual method
    })
  }
  
  # Manual method: Extract p-values from Tukey HSD
  tukey_df <- as.data.frame(tukey_result$social_vuln_category)
  
  # Create a matrix of p-values for all pairwise comparisons
  n_cats <- length(categories)
  p_matrix <- matrix(1, nrow = n_cats, ncol = n_cats)
  rownames(p_matrix) <- categories
  colnames(p_matrix) <- categories
  
  # Fill in p-values from Tukey results
  for(i in seq_len(nrow(tukey_df))) {
    # Try contrast column first (emmeans format), then rownames
    if("contrast" %in% names(tukey_df)) {
      comparison <- as.character(tukey_df$contrast[i])
    } else {
      comparison <- rownames(tukey_df)[i]
    }
    
    # Handle different formats: "High-Low", "High - Low", etc.
    comparison_clean <- trimws(comparison)
    # Try splitting on " - " first (emmeans format), then "-", then ":"
    if(grepl(" - ", comparison_clean)) {
      parts <- strsplit(comparison_clean, " - ")[[1]]
    } else if(grepl("-", comparison_clean)) {
      parts <- strsplit(comparison_clean, "-")[[1]]
    } else if(grepl(":", comparison_clean)) {
      parts <- strsplit(comparison_clean, ":")[[1]]
    } else {
      parts <- NULL
    }
    
    if(!is.null(parts) && length(parts) >= 2) {
      cat1 <- trimws(parts[1])
      cat2 <- trimws(parts[length(parts)])
      # Get p-value - try different column names
      if("p adj" %in% names(tukey_df)) {
        p_val <- tukey_df$`p adj`[i]
      } else if("p.value" %in% names(tukey_df)) {
        p_val <- tukey_df$p.value[i]
      } else if("p" %in% names(tukey_df)) {
        p_val <- tukey_df$p[i]
      } else {
        p_val <- 1
      }
      
      # Handle NA p-values
      if(is.na(p_val)) p_val <- 1
      
      if(cat1 %in% categories && cat2 %in% categories) {
        p_matrix[cat1, cat2] <- p_val
        p_matrix[cat2, cat1] <- p_val
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Assign letters using compact letter display
  # Groups that are NOT significantly different (p > 0.05) share letters
  # Start with all groups getting unique letters
  letters_result <- LETTERS[1:n_cats]
  names(letters_result) <- categories
  
  # Build equivalence groups: groups that are not significantly different share letters
  # Use a simple transitive closure approach
  for(iter in 1:n_cats) {  # Multiple passes to ensure transitive closure
    for(i in 1:(n_cats-1)) {
      for(j in (i+1):n_cats) {
        cat1 <- categories[i]
        cat2 <- categories[j]
        # If not significantly different, they should share the same letter
        if(p_matrix[cat1, cat2] > 0.05) {
          # Use the earlier letter (alphabetically)
          if(which(LETTERS == letters_result[cat1]) > which(LETTERS == letters_result[cat2])) {
            letters_result[cat1] <- letters_result[cat2]
          } else {
            letters_result[cat2] <- letters_result[cat1]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Simplify to sequential letters starting from A
  unique_letters <- sort(unique(letters_result))
  letter_map <- setNames(LETTERS[1:length(unique_letters)], unique_letters)
  for(i in seq_along(letters_result)) {
    letters_result[i] <- letter_map[letters_result[i]]
  }
  
  return(letters_result)
}

# PM2.5 ANCOVA (controlling for covariates)
pm25_tukey <- NULL
pm25_sig_letters <- NULL
pm25_emmeans <- NULL
if(nrow(pm25_worst_month_data) > 0) {
  # Prepare data - ensure covariates are available and not NA
  pm25_model_data <- pm25_worst_month_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(aqi_pm25_corrected) & 
           !is.na(population_density) & 
           !is.na(land_use_type) & 
           !is.na(social_vuln_category))
  
  if(nrow(pm25_model_data) > 0) {
    # Fit ANCOVA model controlling for covariates (if factors have 2+ levels)
    sv_levels <- n_distinct(pm25_model_data$social_vuln_category)
    lu_levels <- n_distinct(pm25_model_data$land_use_type)
    
    if (sv_levels >= 2 && lu_levels >= 2) {
      pm25_ancova <- lm(aqi_pm25_corrected ~ social_vuln_category + 
                        population_density + land_use_type, 
                        data = pm25_model_data)
      pm25_ancova_summary <- summary(pm25_ancova)
      pm25_anova_table <- anova(pm25_ancova)
      
      cat("PM2.5 ANCOVA (", as.character(worst_month_pm25$month_name), ") - Controlling for population_density, land_use_type:\n")
      print(pm25_anova_table)
      cat("\nModel coefficients:\n")
      print(pm25_ancova_summary$coefficients)
      
      # Use emmeans for adjusted means and pairwise comparisons
      if(requireNamespace("emmeans", quietly = TRUE)) {
        pm25_emmeans <- emmeans::emmeans(pm25_ancova, ~ social_vuln_category)
      pm25_pairs <- pairs(pm25_emmeans, adjust = "tukey")
      
      cat("\nPM2.5 Adjusted means (controlling for covariates):\n")
      print(pm25_emmeans)
      
      cat("\nPM2.5 Pairwise comparisons (Tukey HSD, adjusted for covariates):\n")
      print(pm25_pairs)
      
      # Extract p-values for significance letters
      pairs_df <- as.data.frame(pm25_pairs)
      
      # Handle non-estimable comparisons (remove rows with nonEst or NA p-values)
      if("p.value" %in% names(pairs_df)) {
        # Convert character "nonEst" to NA
        if(is.character(pairs_df$p.value)) {
          pairs_df$p.value[pairs_df$p.value == "nonEst"] <- NA
        }
        # Convert to numeric, handling any remaining character values
        pairs_df$p.value <- as.numeric(pairs_df$p.value)
      }
      
      # Note about overall vs pairwise significance
      # Safely extract ANOVA p-value for social_vuln_category (Df == 2)
      anova_p_value <- tryCatch({
        pval <- pm25_anova_table[pm25_anova_table$Df == 2, "Pr(>F)"]
        if(length(pval) == 0) {
          NA_real_
        } else if(length(pval) > 1) {
          pval[1]  # Take first if multiple matches
        } else {
          as.numeric(pval)
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        NA_real_
      })
      
      # Check if we have valid p-values for comparison
      has_valid_pairwise <- any(!is.na(pairs_df$p.value)) && any(pairs_df$p.value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
      has_valid_anova <- !is.na(anova_p_value) && is.finite(anova_p_value)
      
      if(has_valid_anova && anova_p_value < 0.05 && !has_valid_pairwise) {
        cat("\nNOTE: Overall ANCOVA shows significant effect of social vulnerability (p =", 
            round(anova_p_value, 4), 
            "), but no pairwise comparisons are significant after Tukey adjustment.\n")
        cat("This can occur when the effect is distributed across groups rather than concentrated in specific pairs,\n")
        cat("or when multiple testing correction makes pairwise tests more conservative.\n")
      }
      # Create a Tukey-like structure for the significance letter function
      pm25_tukey <- list(social_vuln_category = pairs_df)
      rownames(pm25_tukey$social_vuln_category) <- as.character(pairs_df$contrast)
      # Ensure p adj column exists
      if("p.value" %in% names(pairs_df)) {
        pm25_tukey$social_vuln_category$`p adj` <- pairs_df$p.value
      } else {
        pm25_tukey$social_vuln_category$`p adj` <- rep(1, nrow(pairs_df))
      }
      
      # Get significance letters - only if there are significant differences
      if(any(pairs_df$p.value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)) {
        pm25_sig_letters <- get_significance_letters(pm25_tukey, levels(pm25_model_data$social_vuln_category))
        # Check if all letters are the same - if so, no significant differences to display
        if(length(unique(pm25_sig_letters)) == 1) {
          pm25_sig_letters <- NULL
        }
      } else {
        # No significant differences - set to NULL so no letters are shown
        pm25_sig_letters <- NULL
        cat("\nNo significant differences detected in pairwise comparisons. Skipping letters.\n")
      }
    } # end if emmeans
  } else {
    cat("Insufficient factor levels for PM2.5 ANCOVA (needed 2+ levels for both social_vuln_category and land_use_type).\n")
  }
  cat("\n")
}
}

# Prepare data for plotting with proper error bar limits and label positioning
publishable_disparities_data <- vuln_summary_combined %>%
  mutate(
    pollutant = factor(pollutant, levels = c("PM2.5", "PM10", "Ozone")),
    social_vuln_category = factor(social_vuln_category, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High")),
    # Ensure error bars don't go below 0 (AQI can't be negative)
    error_min = pmax(0, mean_aqi - sd_aqi),
    error_max = mean_aqi + sd_aqi,
    # Ensure sig_letter is not empty - use empty string if NA
    sig_letter = ifelse(is.na(sig_letter) | sig_letter == "", "", sig_letter)
  ) %>%
  # Calculate max values per pollutant for proper y-axis scaling
  group_by(pollutant) %>%
  mutate(
    max_error = max(error_max, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Position value labels just above error bars
    value_y_pos = error_max + (max_error * 0.03),
    # Position significance letters above value labels
    sig_y_pos = error_max + (max_error * 0.08),
    # Position for significance brackets
    bracket_y_pos = error_max + (max_error * 0.12)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Function to extract significant comparisons and create bracket data
create_significance_brackets <- function(pairs_result, pollutant_name, category_levels) {
  if(is.null(pairs_result)) return(data.frame())
  
  pairs_df <- as.data.frame(pairs_result)
  if(!"p.value" %in% names(pairs_df) && !"p adj" %in% names(pairs_df)) return(data.frame())
  
  p_col <- if("p.value" %in% names(pairs_df)) "p.value" else "p adj"
  
  # Get significant comparisons - ensure contrast column exists
  if(!"contrast" %in% names(pairs_df)) {
    # Try to use rownames if contrast column doesn't exist
    pairs_df$contrast <- rownames(pairs_df)
  }
  
  # Get significant comparisons with p-values
  sig_data <- pairs_df %>%
    filter(!!sym(p_col) < 0.05, !is.na(!!sym(p_col))) %>%
    dplyr::select(contrast, p_value = !!sym(p_col))
  
  if(nrow(sig_data) == 0) return(data.frame())
  
  # Parse comparisons and create bracket data
  bracket_list <- list()
  
  for(i in 1:nrow(sig_data)) {
    comp <- sig_data$contrast[i]
    p_val <- sig_data$p_value[i]
    
    comp_str <- as.character(trimws(comp))
    # Parse "High - Moderate" format (emmeans uses " - ")
    if(grepl(" - ", comp_str)) {
      parts <- strsplit(comp_str, " - ")[[1]]
    } else if(grepl("-", comp_str)) {
      parts <- strsplit(comp_str, "-")[[1]]
    } else {
      next
    }
    
    if(length(parts) >= 2) {
      cat1 <- trimws(parts[1])
      cat2 <- trimws(parts[length(parts)])
      
      if(cat1 %in% category_levels && cat2 %in% category_levels) {
        # Create significance indicator
        sig_indicator <- ifelse(p_val < 0.001, "***",
                       ifelse(p_val < 0.01, "**",
                       ifelse(p_val < 0.05, "*", "")))
        
        # Format p-value label
        p_label <- ifelse(p_val < 0.001, "<0.001", 
                 ifelse(p_val < 0.01, paste0("=", sprintf("%.3f", p_val)),
                 paste0("=", sprintf("%.3f", p_val))))
        
        bracket_list[[length(bracket_list) + 1]] <- data.frame(
          pollutant = pollutant_name,
          x_start = cat1,
          x_end = cat2,
          cat1 = cat1,
          cat2 = cat2,
          p_value = p_val,
          sig_indicator = sig_indicator,
          p_label = p_label,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      }
    }
  }
  
  if(length(bracket_list) == 0) return(data.frame())
  
  bracket_data <- bind_rows(bracket_list)
  return(bracket_data)
}

# Create bracket data for each pollutant
pm25_brackets <- if(exists("pm25_pairs") && !is.null(pm25_pairs)) {
  create_significance_brackets(pm25_pairs, "PM2.5", c("Low", "Moderate", "High"))
} else {
  data.frame()
}

pm10_brackets <- if(exists("pm10_pairs") && !is.null(pm10_pairs)) {
  create_significance_brackets(pm10_pairs, "PM10", c("Low", "Moderate", "High"))
} else {
  data.frame()
}

ozone_brackets <- if(exists("ozone_pairs") && !is.null(ozone_pairs)) {
  create_significance_brackets(ozone_pairs, "Ozone", c("Low", "Moderate", "High"))
} else {
  data.frame()
}

# Combine all brackets
all_brackets <- bind_rows(pm25_brackets, pm10_brackets, ozone_brackets)

# Add y positions for brackets based on max error per pollutant
# Convert category names to factor positions for plotting
# Handle multiple brackets per pollutant by stacking them vertically
if(nrow(all_brackets) > 0) {
  all_brackets <- all_brackets %>%
    mutate(
      pollutant = factor(pollutant, levels = c("PM2.5", "PM10", "Ozone")),
      # Convert category names to factor positions (Low=1, Moderate=2, High=3)
      x_start_num = match(x_start, c("Low", "Moderate", "High")),
      x_end_num = match(x_end, c("Low", "Moderate", "High")),
      # Ensure x_start < x_end for proper bracket direction
      x_min = pmin(x_start_num, x_end_num),
      x_max = pmax(x_start_num, x_end_num)
    ) %>%
    # Group by pollutant and assign bracket levels (stack vertically if multiple)
    group_by(pollutant) %>%
    arrange(x_min, x_max) %>%
    mutate(
      bracket_level = row_number(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    # Join with max error values to calculate y positions
    left_join(
      publishable_disparities_data %>%
        group_by(pollutant) %>%
        summarise(base_y = max(error_max, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
      by = "pollutant"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Position brackets: first at 15% above max, subsequent at +6% increments
      bracket_y = base_y * (1.15 + (bracket_level - 1) * 0.06),
      # Vertical line height (tick marks) - make them more visible
      tick_height = base_y * 0.02
    )
}

publishable_disparities <- publishable_disparities_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = social_vuln_category, y = mean_aqi, fill = social_vuln_category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = error_min, ymax = error_max), 
                width = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8, color = "gray40") +
  # Value labels
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(mean_aqi, 1)), y = value_y_pos), 
            vjust = 0, 
            size = 3.8, 
            fontface = "bold",
            color = "gray25") +
  # Significance letters - only show when there are significant differences
  geom_text(data = publishable_disparities_data %>% filter(sig_letter != "" & !is.na(sig_letter)),
            aes(label = sig_letter, y = sig_y_pos), 
            vjust = 0, 
            size = 5.5, 
            fontface = "bold",
            color = "black") +
  # Significance brackets - show bars connecting significant pairs
  {if(nrow(all_brackets) > 0) {
    all_brackets_with_levels <- all_brackets %>%
      mutate(
        x_min_factor = factor(c("Low", "Moderate", "High")[x_min], levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High")),
        x_max_factor = factor(c("Low", "Moderate", "High")[x_max], levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High"))
      )
    list(
      # Horizontal line connecting the two categories
      geom_segment(data = all_brackets_with_levels,
                   aes(x = as.numeric(x_min_factor), xend = as.numeric(x_max_factor), y = bracket_y, yend = bracket_y),
                   inherit.aes = FALSE,
                   color = "black",
                   linewidth = 1.2),
      # Left vertical line (bracket end/tick)
      geom_segment(data = all_brackets_with_levels,
                   aes(x = as.numeric(x_min_factor), xend = as.numeric(x_min_factor), y = bracket_y, yend = bracket_y - tick_height),
                   inherit.aes = FALSE,
                   color = "black",
                   linewidth = 1.2),
      # Right vertical line (bracket end/tick)
      geom_segment(data = all_brackets_with_levels,
                   aes(x = as.numeric(x_max_factor), xend = as.numeric(x_max_factor), y = bracket_y, yend = bracket_y - tick_height),
                   inherit.aes = FALSE,
                   color = "black",
                   linewidth = 1.2),
      # P-value labels above brackets
      geom_text(data = all_brackets_with_levels,
                aes(x = (as.numeric(x_min_factor) + as.numeric(x_max_factor)) / 2, y = bracket_y, label = paste0("p", p_label, sig_indicator)),
                inherit.aes = FALSE,
                vjust = -0.3,
                size = 3.5,

# PUBLISHABLE GRAPHIC 2: Percentage difference from Low vulnerability areas
# Calculate pct_diff_from_low explicitly in a separate step
vuln_summary_for_pct <- vuln_summary_combined %>%
  group_by(pollutant) %>%
  mutate(
    low_mean_aqi = mean_aqi[social_vuln_category == "Low"][1]
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    pct_diff_from_low = ifelse(
      !is.na(low_mean_aqi) & low_mean_aqi > 0 & !is.na(mean_aqi),
      round(100 * (mean_aqi - low_mean_aqi) / low_mean_aqi, 1),
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-low_mean_aqi) %>%
  filter(social_vuln_category != "Low" & !is.na(pct_diff_from_low)) %>%
  mutate(
    pollutant = factor(pollutant, levels = c("PM2.5", "PM10", "Ozone")),
    social_vuln_category = factor(social_vuln_category, levels = c("Moderate", "High")),
    # Pre-calculate label and vjust to avoid issues in ggplot
    label_text = paste0(round(pct_diff_from_low, 1), "%"),
    label_vjust = ifelse(pct_diff_from_low >= 0, -0.5, 1.5)
  )

publishable_pct_diff <- vuln_summary_for_pct %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = social_vuln_category, y = pct_diff_from_low, fill = social_vuln_category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", linewidth = 1, color = "gray50") +

            size = 4.5, 
            fontface = "bold",

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("High" = "#D55E00", "Moderate" = "#F59E42"),
    name = "Social Vulnerability\nCategory",
    labels = c("High" = "High", "Moderate" = "Moderate")

  labs(

  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),

  ) +
```

# Cumulative Disparity Analysis
```{r cumulative_disparity}
cat("\n=============================================================================\n")
cat("CUMULATIVE DISPARITY ANALYSIS\n")
cat("=============================================================================\n\n")

# Calculate site-day level exceedances
cumulative_disparity <- daily_avg %>%
  filter(!is.na(aqi_pm25_corrected), !is.na(social_vuln_category)) %>%
  mutate(
    aqi_pm25_corrected = ifelse(aqi_pm25_corrected < 0, 0, aqi_pm25_corrected),
    exceeds_50  = aqi_pm25_corrected > 50,
    exceeds_100 = aqi_pm25_corrected > 100
  ) %>%
  group_by(social_vuln_category) %>%
  summarise(
    total_person_days   = n(),
    days_exceed_50      = sum(exceeds_50,  na.rm = TRUE),
    days_exceed_100     = sum(exceeds_100, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_exceed_50       = round(100 * days_exceed_50  / total_person_days, 1),
    pct_exceed_100      = round(100 * days_exceed_100 / total_person_days, 1),
    mean_aqi_pm25       = round(mean(aqi_pm25_corrected,   na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    median_aqi_pm25     = round(median(aqi_pm25_corrected, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(factor(social_vuln_category, levels = c("High", "Moderate", "Low")))

cat("Cumulative disparity summary by social vulnerability category:\n\n")
kable(cumulative_disparity,
      col.names = c("Social Vulnerability", "Total Person-Days",
                    "Days > AQI 50", "Days > AQI 100",
                    "% Days > AQI 50", "% Days > AQI 100",
                    "Mean AQI (PM2.5)", "Median AQI (PM2.5)"),
      caption = "Cumulative PM2.5 AQI exposure by social vulnerability category") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)

# Bar chart: % days exceeding AQI 50 by social vulnerability category
vuln_colors <- c("High" = "#D55E00", "Moderate" = "#0072B2", "Low" = "#009E73")

cumulative_disparity_plot <- ggplot(
  cumulative_disparity,
  aes(x = factor(social_vuln_category, levels = c("High", "Moderate", "Low")),
      y = pct_exceed_50,
      fill = social_vuln_category)
) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct_exceed_50, "%")),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = vuln_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Social vulnerability category",
    y = "Percentage of days with PM2.5 AQI > 50 (%)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text  = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    plot.margin = margin(20, 20, 20, 20)
  )

print(cumulative_disparity_plot)
```

```{r raincloud_plot, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=7.5}
# ==============================================================================
# Raincloud plot figure of AQI PM2.5 by HOLC housing grade
# ==============================================================================

# Helper function to format numbers to specific significant figures
format_sig_figs <- function(x, n = 2) {
  s <- formatC(signif(x, n), digits = n, format = "g", flag = "#")
  sub("[.]$", "", s)
}

# Clean and prepare data for PM2.5
pm25_data <- daily_avg %>%
  filter(!is.na(housing_grade) & !is.na(aqi_pm25_corrected)) %>%
  mutate(aqi_pm25_corrected = ifelse(aqi_pm25_corrected < 0, 0, aqi_pm25_corrected)) %>%
  label_housing_grades() %>%
  mutate(housing_grade_label = factor(housing_grade_label, 
                                      levels = c("D: Hazardous", "C: Declining", "Not Graded", "IC: Industrial")))

# Print statistics of data points and sites per HOLC grade
pm25_summary_stats <- pm25_data %>%
  group_by(housing_grade_label) %>%
  summarise(
    n_observations = n(),
    n_sites = n_distinct(site),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )
cat("\n=== PM2.5 DATA STATS PER HOLC GRADE ===\n")
print(pm25_summary_stats)
cat("=======================================\n\n")

# Tukey letters using the existing run_redlining_anova() function
pm25_anova <- run_redlining_anova(pm25_data, "aqi_pm25_corrected")

# Format Tukey letters for PM2.5
pm25_letters <- pm25_anova$letters %>%
  mutate(housing_grade_label = case_when(
    group == "C" ~ "C: Declining",
    group == "D" ~ "D: Hazardous",
    group == "IC" ~ "IC: Industrial",
    group == "Not Graded" ~ "Not Graded",
    TRUE ~ as.character(group)
  )) %>%
  mutate(housing_grade_label = factor(housing_grade_label, 
                                      levels = c("D: Hazardous", "C: Declining", "Not Graded", "IC: Industrial")))

ref_mean_pm25 <- mean(pm25_data$aqi_pm25_corrected[pm25_data$housing_grade_label == "Not Graded"], na.rm = TRUE)

# ── 2. Per-grade summary ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
grade_stats_pm25 <- pm25_data %>%
  group_by(housing_grade_label) %>%
  summarise(
    grade_mean = mean(aqi_pm25_corrected, na.rm = TRUE),
    peak_density = max(density(aqi_pm25_corrected, na.rm = TRUE)$y),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    diff = grade_mean - ref_mean_pm25,
    delta_label = case_when(
      housing_grade_label == "Not Graded" ~ "Δ0",
      diff > 0 ~ sprintf("Δ+%s", format_sig_figs(diff, 2)),
      diff < 0 ~ sprintf("Δ−%s", format_sig_figs(abs(diff), 2)),
      TRUE ~ "Δ±0"
    ),
    label_x = (grade_mean + ref_mean_pm25) / 2,
    xmin = pmin(grade_mean, ref_mean_pm25),
    xmax = pmax(grade_mean, ref_mean_pm25)
  )

# ── 3. Build plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
raincloud_fig <- ggplot(pm25_data, aes(x = aqi_pm25_corrected)) +
  # Filled density
  geom_density(
    aes(fill = housing_grade_label, color = housing_grade_label),
    alpha = 0.82, linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  # Gap shading — grades exceeding Not Graded mean (panel's existing fill color at alpha=0.3)
  geom_rect(
    data = dplyr::filter(grade_stats_pm25, grade_mean > ref_mean_pm25),
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = housing_grade_label),
    alpha = 0.3,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  # Gap shading — grades below/equal to Not Graded mean (neutral gray at alpha=0.3)
  geom_rect(
    data = dplyr::filter(grade_stats_pm25, grade_mean <= ref_mean_pm25),
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    fill = "grey50",
    alpha = 0.3,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  # Not Graded mean — dashed grey, behind grade line
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = ref_mean_pm25,
    linetype   = "dashed",
    color      = "grey50",
    linewidth  = 0.5
  ) +
  # Grade mean — solid, grade-colored, on top
  geom_vline(
    data = grade_stats_pm25,
    aes(xintercept = grade_mean, color = housing_grade_label),
    linetype    = "solid",
    linewidth   = 0.9,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  # Delta label showing difference from Not Graded mean — just to the right of the solid mean line, at the top of density curve
  geom_text(
    data  = grade_stats_pm25,
    aes(x = grade_mean, y = peak_density,
        label = delta_label),
    vjust       = -1.0,
    hjust       = -0.40,
    size        = 5.0,
    fontface    = "plain",
    color       = "grey10",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = holc_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = holc_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 65),
    breaks = seq(0, 60, by = 10),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.10))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.40))) +
  facet_wrap(~ housing_grade_label, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = expression("Daily Mean PM"["2.5"] ~ "AQI"),
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    strip.text        = element_text(size = 12, face = "plain", color = "grey15",
                                     hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 4)),
    strip.background  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x       = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey15", face = "plain",
                                     margin = margin(t = 3)),
    axis.text.y       = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y      = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y       = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y      = element_blank(),
    axis.line.x       = element_line(color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.ticks.x      = element_line(color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(2.5, "pt"),
    axis.title.x      = element_text(size = 13, color = "grey10", face = "plain",
                                     margin = margin(t = 6)),
    panel.spacing     = unit(1.4, "lines"),
    panel.background  = element_blank(),
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin       = margin(t = 5, r = 5, b = 5, l = 15)
  )

# Create output folder if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists("figures")) {
  dir.create("figures", recursive = TRUE)
}

# Save results
ggsave("figures/raincloud_holc_aqi.pdf", plot = raincloud_fig, device = cairo_pdf, width = 6.9, height = 7.5)
ggsave("figures/raincloud_holc_aqi.png", plot = raincloud_fig, width = 6.9, height = 7.5, dpi = 300)

print(raincloud_fig)
```

Figure X. Daily Mean PM2.5 AQI Distribution by Historical HOLC Housing Grade. Raincloud plots show the distribution of daily mean sensor-corrected PM2.5 AQI values across the four historical HOLC redlining groups: Grade C: Declining (yellow), Grade D: Hazardous (red), Grade IC: Industrial/Commercial (orange), and Not Graded (grey) ($N = 2,478$ total site-day observations across 472 unique calendar days and 15 monitoring sites). Half-density plots (clouds) display the probability distribution of AQI values, and embedded box plots illustrate the median, interquartile range (IQR), and 1.5 × IQR whiskers for each group. Compact letter displays (a, b) in the upper right of each panel indicate statistically significant differences; groups sharing a letter are not significantly different at the $p < 0.05$ level based on post-hoc Tukey HSD comparisons from an ANCOVA model controlling for population density ($F_{(3, 2473)} = 7.56, p < 0.001$). Grade IC (Industrial/Commercial) exhibits the lowest levels of PM2.5 exposure (Tukey group 'b'), while all other categories exhibit higher exposure (Tukey group 'a').

Figure X. Daily Mean Air Temperature Distribution by Historical HOLC Housing Grade. Small multiples density plots represent the distribution of daily mean air temperature (°C) across the four historical HOLC redlining groups: Grade C: Declining (yellow), Grade D: Hazardous (red), Grade IC: Industrial (orange), and Not Graded (grey) ($N = 2,471$ total site-day observations across 476 unique calendar days and 15 monitoring sites). Solid vertical lines denote the mean daily temperature for each group, while the dashed grey line represents the baseline mean temperature of the Not Graded reference group ($15.8^{\circ}\text{C}$). The shaded rectangular bands and annotated delta values ($\Delta$) highlight the temperature difference of each group relative to this baseline. Compact letter displays (a, b) in the upper right of each panel indicate statistically significant differences; groups sharing a letter are not significantly different at the $p < 0.05$ level based on post-hoc Tukey HSD comparisons from an ANCOVA model controlling for population density ($F_{(3, 2466)} = 9.62, p < 0.001$). Grades C and D exhibit the highest thermal exposure, exceeding the Not Graded baseline by $+1.71^{\circ}\text{C}$ and $+2.55^{\circ}\text{C}$ respectively, while Grade IC is comparable to non-graded areas ($+0.147^{\circ}\text{C}$ difference).

```{r daily_aqi_timeline, fig.width=16, fig.height=3.8}
# ── 1. Prep ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Filter daily data to December 2024 through March 2026
daily_site <- daily_avg %>%
  filter(timestamp_day >= as.Date("2024-12-01") & timestamp_day <= as.Date("2026-03-31")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  dplyr::select(date = timestamp_day, site, pm25_aqi = aqi_pm25_corrected, pm10_aqi = aqi_pm10_corrected)

# Compute daily statistics (mean, min, max) for ribbon and lines (without warnings)
daily_summary <- daily_site %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    pm25_mean = if(all(is.na(pm25_aqi))) NA_real_ else mean(pm25_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    pm25_min  = if(all(is.na(pm25_aqi))) NA_real_ else min(pm25_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    pm25_max  = if(all(is.na(pm25_aqi))) NA_real_ else max(pm25_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    pm10_mean = if(all(is.na(pm10_aqi))) NA_real_ else mean(pm10_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    pm10_min  = if(all(is.na(pm10_aqi))) NA_real_ else min(pm10_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    pm10_max  = if(all(is.na(pm10_aqi))) NA_real_ else max(pm10_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Compute dynamic y-axis limit (1.1 * max observed AQI)
max_observed_aqi <- max(c(daily_site$pm25_aqi, daily_site$pm10_aqi), na.rm = TRUE)
nn_ylim <- 1.1 * max_observed_aqi

# desaturated tonal washes for AQI bands
aqi_bands <- tibble::tribble(
  ~ymin, ~ymax, ~fill,
  0,   50,  "#D4E8C2",   # Good
  50,  100, "#FAEDB4",   # Moderate
  100, 150, "#F8D3A8",   # Sensitive Groups
  150, 500, "#F2BDB8"    # Unhealthy
)

# Date limits for x-axis
start_date <- as.Date("2024-12-01")
end_date <- as.Date("2026-03-31")
scale_end_date <- as.Date("2026-06-15")

# Sensor calibration gap range
cal_start <- as.Date("2025-11-01")
cal_end <- as.Date("2026-01-31")

# Base theme (Matched to SVI timeline graphic, base_size = 14, plot.title margin.b = 4)
common_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14, margin = margin(b = 4)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey20"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13, color = "grey15", margin = margin(r = 6)),
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.35),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey20", angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.35),
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey92", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  )



# ── 2. Build panels ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Panel (a) PM2.5 Plot
p_pm25 <- ggplot() +
  # 1. AQI category bands (bottom layer, alpha lowered to 0.35)
  geom_rect(
    data = aqi_bands,
    aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    xmin = start_date, xmax = end_date,
    fill = aqi_bands$fill,
    alpha = 0.35,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  # 2. Uncertainty Ribbon (Sensor Range, alpha bumped to 0.5)
  geom_ribbon(

  ) +

  geom_segment(

    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.3,

  ) +
```
